answer: A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. The umber multiplier is published, charged in copper, and lantern lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2665 identities would post 829 proofs and burn roughly 24 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
